assertions.text: Documented features include a Hyper-Parallel Browser, MCP Hive toolsets per agent, Swarm Bridge backend integration, ThoughtStream reasoning visualization, Local Token Optimizer, Data Fusion Engine, and Multimodal Swarm Vision.
The Swarm Bridge exposes an Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible API so the swarm can serve as a backend for Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenClaw, per the documentation.
The product is described as a native Windows and macOS desktop app coordinating up to 300 parallel AI sub-agents, powered by Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.7 Code model.
Documentation states each agent carries a full MCP toolset covering files, browser, databases, and APIs, with up to 1,500+ tool calls claimed in the comparison table.
The documentation cites benchmark figures for the underlying model: 81.1% on MCPMark Verified versus Claude Opus 4.8's 76.4%, and 62.0 on Kimi Code Bench v2, up from K2.6's 50.9.
Repository development practice: the docs suggest building from source to verify release integrity, and the repository is MIT-licensed with source, releases, and issues hosted on GitHub.

The docs describe a proprietary 'PARL' coordination layer for sub-agent synergy and 'Critical Steps' routing that auto-detects critical task nodes and allocates compute there, reportedly cutting runtime up to 80%.
The desktop UI reportedly includes a live side-panel task map showing all agents' reasoning, page reads, and code edits in real time via ThoughtStream.

The app depends on Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.7 Code model (1T-parameter MoE, ~32B active per token, 256K context, open weights on Hugging Face), and Swarm mode routes requests through a built-in proxy pool.

The disclaimer states the app is an independent third-party product not affiliated with or endorsed by Moonshot AI, and that performance figures reflect benchmark conditions with real-world results varying by task, hardware, and network.
The app is positioned as a one-click installer requiring no terminal, with heavy computation on a cloud cluster while the desktop acts as orchestrator (8GB RAM stated as sufficient).
kimi-k2-7/kimi-k2.7 is mentioned in this evidence.
